Title: EC: No proposal to increase Sarawak parliamentary seats
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Election Commission (EC) said there is currently no proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak, contrary to a local newspaper report linking the matter to discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the report cited a purported document on the proposed redelineation of Sarawak's parliamentary constituencies, which the newspaper claimed to have obtained.
"The EC has only prepared recommendations for the Seventh Sarawak Electoral Constituency Redelineation Review, which are currently on public display throughout this month," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril advised the newspaper to refer to authentic and accurate information on the redelineation exercise through the EC's official portal or statements.
The local Malay-language newspaper had earlier reported that the proposed redelineation exercise would see the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak increase from 31 to 46, citing a document purportedly outlining the exercise.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas prepares to contest Bersatu-held Kuala Sentul, Lepar
Article:
KUANTAN: Pas has begun preparations to contest the Kuala Sentul and Lepar state seats, which were won by Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 15th general election (GE15).
Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said there was
no longer an alliance
between Pas and Bersatu following the split between the two parties, while the assemblymen for both seats now support the Barisan Nasional (BN) state government.
"During the last general election, both constituencies were won under the PN logo. The split between Pas and Bersatu means any party has the right to contest the seats.
"Since the previous victories were secured under the PN banner, Pas is also entitled to field candidates in the constituencies in the 16th general election (GE16). Furthermore, a large part of the machinery that worked towards PN's victories in both constituencies comprised Pas members and supporters," he said in a Facebook post today.
Rosli said Pahang Pas had already begun its groundwork, with several programmes carried out and more planned.
"Everything is in place for Pas Pahang to contest both seats, including its election machinery, funding, schedules and the best candidates. All preparations have been made in detail.
"Pas is confident that voters in Kuala Sentul and Lepar will side with the party, based on the strong commitment shown by all Pas state assemblymen and members of parliament in Pahang in carrying out their mandates despite limited funding," he said.
Following GE15, Pahang PN had 17 elected representatives — 15 from Pas and two from Bersatu. The two Bersatu assemblymen are Lepar assemblyman Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus and Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaludin.
However, last month, Yazid and Jasri
pledged their support for
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and backed his administration until GE16.
Lepar is under the Umno-led Paya Besar parliamentary constituency, while Kuala Sentul falls under the Pas-led Maran parliamentary constituency.
In GE15, BN and PN each won 17 seats in the Pahang Legislative Assembly, while Pakatan Harapan secured eight, giving the 42-member assembly its current composition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-army corporal acquitted of 17 charges, including 15 molestation counts
Article:
MELAKA: A former army corporal was acquitted and discharged by the Ayer Keroh magistrate's court here today of 17 charges, including 15 counts of molesting a male recruit at Terendak Camp in 2023.
Magistrate Uthman Abd Ghani made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused, Mohd Amanah Habhijullah, 38.
He said the dates and times for each charge had not been specified, leaving the prosecution case heavily reliant on the evidence of the complainant, who was also the first prosecution witness (SP1).
"The court found that SP1 could not recall the dates of the incidents, while the prosecution alleged that the 15 offences occurred between August and October 2023.
"SP1 could only recall one date, Oct 14, 2023, after referring to the police report," he said when delivering his brief judgment at the end of the prosecution's case today.
Uthman said there were discrepancies between SP1's police report and his testimony in court, particularly concerning the accused's actions after the alleged incident on Oct 14, 2023.
He said the court also found discrepancies in the evidence relating to two charges involving causing injury, including the allegation that the accused hit SP1 with a broomstick and kicked him in the chest on Oct 15, 2023.
According to Uthman, the testimonies of several witnesses concerning the incident differed, including on whether SP1 was hit on the head, whether the broomstick broke and whether there was any bleeding.
"For the 17th charge, there were also discrepancies concerning the presence of another witness at the scene.
"SP1 initially said there was another witness, but after the police report was referred to, he said only he and the accused were at the location," he said.
Uthman said although SP1 had experienced trauma and depression following his relationship with the accused, the prosecution case was still riddled with discrepancies and reasonable doubt, and was not supported by sufficient evidence in law.
The court subsequently acquitted and discharged Mohd Amanah of all 17 charges, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case and that it would not be safe to call on the accused to enter his defence.
Deputy public prosecutor Syauqi Mardia Baharudin prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer S Daniel.
After the proceedings, Mohd Amanah appeared emotional and expressed gratitude over the court's decision.
He described the case as defamatory.
"...For 2 years and 4 months, I was disappointed because I was accused. That is why I wanted to fight this case because I knew I was being accused by him (the complainant) without evidence," he said.
A total of 11 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial.
On March 15, 2024, media reported that the accused was first charged in court with 17 offences, including 15 counts of molesting a male army recruit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar wants small traders to suggest aid recipients ahead of 2027 Budget
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants small entrepreneurs in every village to propose fellow traders who should receive government assistance under the planned increase in allocation for the group in 2027 Budget.
He said the suggestions were important to ensure aid reached small traders who genuinely needed it and had the potential to expand their businesses.
"I want to give small traders in every village the opportunity to suggest if there are other friends who should be given a chance... because in our Budget next month, God willing, I want to increase the allocation for these entrepreneurs," he said when officiating the Kedah Usahawan Bangkit scheme at the Federal Government Administration Complex in Anak Bukit here today.
Anwar said many stalls run by small entrepreneurs also provided employment, helping to generate income for the local community.
"When we give aid to these small entrepreneurs, even if it is small, they work hard and truly appreciate the assistance given," he added.
About 1,500 entrepreneurs and petty traders in Kedah attended today's event in support of the government's efforts to strengthen the people's economy.
Through the Usahawan Bangkit scheme, the government provides business equipment tailored to entrepreneurs' needs to increase their business capacity and productivity.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue attracting major foreign investments to boost the country's economy while ensuring the entry of foreign companies did not affect local enterprises, particularly small entrepreneurs.
"Although I bring in foreign investments, I do not disrupt small entrepreneurs... I don't go overseas for no reason," he said.
He said investments by major companies, including in artificial intelligence (AI), computing and semiconductors, could stimulate economic growth and create more job opportunities.
Anwar also cited developments in medical technology in China, which he said was capable of treating blindness and restoring sight.
Meanwhile, the prime minister stressed that the government would continue working to ease the people's burden, particularly in addressing the rising cost of goods.

Title: Malaysia calls for greater burden-sharing over Rohingya crisis
Article:
NEW YORK: Malaysia has called for greater burden-sharing and international responsibility to support countries hosting Rohingya refugees amid the prolonged crisis in Myanmar.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said a sustainable solution required efforts to address the root causes of the crisis, including citizenship issues, while creating conditions for Rohingya refugees to return safely, voluntarily and with dignity to their places of origin in Rakhine State.
"Malaysia remains deeply concerned about the prolonged conflict and worsening humanitarian situation in Myanmar, particularly the continued suffering of the Rohingya, which has also had a significant impact on Malaysia," he said.
Speaking during an intervention at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Annual Coordination Meeting of Foreign Ministers on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) today, Mohamad said Malaysia remained committed to efforts to ensure accountability for human rights violations.
He also reiterated Malaysia's support for the case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar at the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
"We welcome the conclusion of the hearings on the merits of the case at the ICJ in January 2026 and look forward to the court's decision," he said.
In support of the legal efforts, Malaysia was also actively contributing to the OIC Fund for Rohingya, Mohamad said.
He also encouraged other OIC member states to contribute generously to the fund.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Between China Glut and increasingly irrational West, Malaysian automotive market is stuck between a rock and a hard place
Article:
SCROLL through any local EV forum or social media comment section today, and you will find a consistent chorus of anger.
When the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry tightened its regulatory stance with protective walls - such as the minimum RM200,000 CIF threshold and 180 kW motor output floors for fully imported (CBU) electric vehicles - the digital reaction was swift and predictable.
The government was accused of shielding legacy dinosaurs, choking the green technology revolution, and locking everyday Malaysians out of affordable mobility.
From the perspective of an individual consumer grappling with the cost-of-living squeeze, that frustration makes complete sense. Who wouldn't want a silent, high-tech, zero-emission vehicle at a sub-RM150,000 price point?
When the low-price bonanza suddenly disappears just as a significant portion of the market is starting to get on board, the instinctive reaction is to blast the policy as bureaucratic gatekeeping.
The optics certainly support the anger.
Then last week, Thailand - which had previously been very bullish on electric vehicles - decided to slam the brakes on imports as well, instituting higher tariffs and even stricter local content requirements for vehicles assembled within their borders.
The "Detroit of Southeast Asia" is fast looking like a manufacturing hub under siege, caught off guard by the faster-than-expected transition toward battery electric vehicles.
As a nation with hardly any proven petroleum reserves, Thailand's push for electrification seemed logical, commendable even.
But three years after the starter gun was fired in 2023, the situation for their domestic automotive industry is looking quite grim.
By June this year, BEVs and hybrids accounted to 55 per cent of all car sales - a number beyond the imagination of policymakers who aimed for 30 per cent of locally made cars to be zero-emission vehicles by 2030.
Once that 30 per cent target was breached last year, and it became clear that the vast majority of ZEVs sold were imported from China, the government knew they had to change the game.
Faced with monumental excess capacity at home, Chinese automakers were forced to export.
They took advantage of whatever state financial incentives they could secure to chase foreign reserves, and went to town with it. This resulted in record car exports from China in 2025, and the trend shows no sign of slowing down.
Australia is now awash with Chinese brands, dominating the EV segment so thoroughly that nearly all non-Tesla competitors have retreated.
Mighty Volkswagen is so battered by the global tsunami that they are looking to cut 100,000 jobs at home and abroad. Things are so bad they sold off Bugatti and are reportedly contemplating letting Ducati go - selling their crown jewels just to keep the lights on.
Thailand and Malaysia have very little by way of home-grown technology to compete with China.
Yet Germany, which essentially dominated automotive engineering for the last century, is now begging Brussels to erect tariff walls just so it can catch its breath.
To be honest, it's hard to overstate the tectonic shift happening in the global auto industry right now, and Thailand's sudden pivot is merely a shockwave from that wider tremor. Any nation with a
domestic supply chain is feeling the heat, starting with the smaller players - local vendors supplying minor components to Tier-1 suppliers.
These outfits, running on razor-thin margins with fewer than 50 workers, can weather a few stormy months. But if orders keep shrinking with no sign of recovery, layoffs become inevitable, with the sobering knowledge that rehiring skilled hands later will not be easy.
Thailand has far more to lose than Malaysia. Their supply chain runs much deeper, and vastly more livelihoods rely on the sector because their installed capacity sits around 2 million units a year - more than double ours.
Furthermore, Thai factories function primarily as heavy export manufacturing bases. With Japanese mainstays like Honda, Mitsubishi, Nissan, and Mazda under global pressure, Thai production output is forced to contract to match market reality.
Malaysia's car factories, by contrast, feed over 90 per cent of their output straight to the domestic market. Because our local components industry calculates local content differently than the Thais, our immediate shocks will be smaller, though still painful.
As our domestic market surged post-pandemic, our automotive component trade deficit ballooned from RM15 billion in 2020 to RM39 billion last year.
Yes, we have local assembly, but not nearly enough true local content. If August sales figures for Proton e.MAS are any indication, the market is finally warming up to battery power.
But looking at Proton alone, it is clear they massively underestimated the shift. When they launched their EV assembly line late last year capped at 20,000 units annually - a paltry number I pointed out at the time - they insisted they had expansion plans to 40,000.
Even that feels conservative. With the e.Mas brand pulling in numbers tracking toward the Saga, they are severely straining against demand.
In the short term, expect them to hunt for excess capacity wherever they can find it. In the medium term, trees are going to have to come down for major factory expansion in Tanjung Malim.
And then we will hit the brick wall of local content.
The uncomfortable truth is that we do not have the manufacturing depth to even come close to fulfilling true local content requirements, even if brands genuinely want to cross every T and dot every I.
For too long, the local component ecosystem has been living a polite fiction. In a desire to accommodate domestic players, authorities allowed modules assembled using foreign child parts to be counted as local content. Decades of such lenient enforcement mean we can no longer even properly enforce our own industrial rules.
So, as we grandstand about defending the local industry, I am haunted by the image of Pak Kaduk - the classic folktale figure who traded away his winning fighting cock right before the main match.
When his former bird won, he cheered wildly, forgetting entirely that the champion had changed hands before the bell rang.
There is still time, but very little.
We need an honest, brutal assessment of our local component suppliers and their true technological capabilities before deciding how to navigate the wild west of the EV transition.
Otherwise, the ministry and enforcement agencies will simply keep inventing creative loopholes to preserve the illusion of policy compliance, while we pretend that all is well.
The rock is global geopolitics that we cannot control. The hard place is entirely of our own making.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yinson privatisation talks continue, indicative price unchanged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Holdings Bhd and MISC Bhd say talks on a potential privatisation of Yinson are ongoing, with the indicative offer price maintained at RM2.35 a share.
In separate Bursa Malaysia filings on Friday, the companies said the proposed deal would be carried out through a scheme of arrangement under Section 366 of the Companies Act 2016.
However, the deal is still subject to further discussions and negotiations, the signing of definitive agreements, a final offer price, as well as regulatory and other required approvals.
Both companies stressed that there is no certainty the talks will result in a deal.
Last month, Yinson said it had received a letter from Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd the investment vehicle of executive chairman Lim Han Weng and his family.
The letter confirmed that Yinson Legacy was in talks with MISC and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to take Yinson private.
If an agreement is reached, MISC and Yinson Legacy would acquire the 55.2 per cent of Yinson shares not already held by Yinson Legacy and parties acting in concert with it.
EPF would retain its existing effective stake in Yinson.
Lim and his family hold a combined 27.68 per cent stake, while EPF owns 17.09 per cent. Retirement Fund Inc, better known as KWAP, holds another 6.7 per cent.
Following completion, MISC and Yinson Legacy are expected to hold equal stakes in Yinson.
Yinson operates eight floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessels, with operations spanning Southeast Asia, South America and Africa.
MISC, which is 51 per cent owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), has six FPSOs and six other vessels operating in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Brazil.
Yinson also has 557 megawatts of renewable energy assets, with another 148MW under construction in India, Peru and New Zealand.
The group also operates electric vehicle charging stations in Malaysia and Singapore.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bandar Utama school stabbing: Victim's family to file civil suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The family of a student who was stabbed at a school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, will file a civil suit and provide full cooperation to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) in its appeal against the case.
The victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, said the family had officially appointed lawyers to initiate civil proceedings against relevant parties to seek accountability, particularly over possible negligence in preventing the incident.
She said the parties to be named in the civil suit would be determined after the family's legal team had reviewed and considered the matter.
"To this day, there is still one question on my mind... could this tragedy really have been prevented?" she said at a press conference here today, which was also attended by Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng.
The A-GC had earlier filed a notice of appeal against the High Court's decision to acquit a 15-year-old boy of a murder charge involving the victim, Yap Shing Xuen.
Meanwhile, Lim said lawyers at his service centre would provide full legal support to the victim's family.
He said his office had also appointed lawyer Chia Hui Ming to assist the deputy public prosecutor in the appeal process.
"On Sept 22, the A-GC officially filed a notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal against the High Court's decision.
"This clearly shows the official position that the High Court's decision is being challenged," he said.
Hui Ming said his team had yet to gain access to important documents related to the case, including witness statements and medical reports.
He said without a comprehensive review of all the evidence, it would not be appropriate for the team to draw any conclusions or interfere with the prosecution's case.
"Moreover, the prosecution has filed an appeal and the matter should be left to the Court of Appeal to make a final decision after reviewing all the evidence," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Talk of US export ban on diesel deepens US crude futures' discount to global benchmark
Article:
HOUSTON: Washington's talk of a possible ban on diesel exports is widening the gap between US crude oil futures and the global Brent benchmark, a signal that markets expect US refiners to process less crude oil if their diesel output gets stuck at home.
While that may bring some immediate relief to high domestic diesel prices, which this week hit a record US$6.528 a gallon and stirred a political uproar, the bigger discount for domestic crude futures could be a double-edged omen: an indicator of higher gasoline prices to come, while in the longer term diesel prices could also begin rising again.
As investors price in a scenario where diesel gets stranded in the US, West Texas Intermediate crude futures traded as much as US$12.02 a barrel under Brent futures on Thursday, their largest discount since May 6, according to LSEG data.
Analysts say US refiners could cut their crude runs by as much as 12 per cent if diesel exports are banned, with key storage hubs likely to fill up within a month.
The US is the world's largest diesel exporter, with net exports of about 1.2 million barrels per day, versus production of 5.1 million bpd, according to Morgan Stanley.
These exports have partially plugged the gap from lost Middle East barrels while the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. Diesel supplies have also dwindled from Russia, which has repeatedly imposed export bans of its own to tackle shortages that followed Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil refineries.
Wood Mackenzie analysts, in a note on Thursday, said a diesel export ban would redirect a 700,000 bpd oversupply of diesel and gasoil into storage, effectively filling Gulf Coast inventories to maximum capacity in just over a month.
That would force US refiners to cut crude runs by more than 2 million bpd, Wood Mackenzie estimated, to prevent inventories from exceeding capacity — a reduction of 12 per cent of US refinery crude runs at current rates.
The prospects for a US diesel export ban remain uncertain.
The White House on Wednesday denied media reports it was preparing for a 90-day diesel export ban, and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said a ban would not bring surging prices under control. On Tuesday, however, President Donald Trump said he backed a ban.
In the meantime, Wright has contacted executives at several major American refiners in recent days to gauge support for voluntary restraint on diesel exports, as the Trump administration searches for an alternative to a short-term ban, according to three people familiar with the discussions.
RECORD DIESEL PRICES STIR CALLS FOR EXPORT BAN
Driving the demand for a US export ban is a surge in diesel prices, which have hit records in both the US and Europe. On Thursday, US prices remained elevated at US$6.514 a gallon, according to the AAA, as the US war with Iran disrupts global supplies.
That could spell trouble for Trump's Republican Party in the November midterm elections, by fuelling inflation and putting a particularly heavy burden on farmers, one of the party's key constituencies.
The Iran war is complicating the conundrum in the US oil sector in another way: by boosting shipping costs.
A rise in the discount for US crude relative to European crude, known as the WTI-Brent spread, typically boosts demand for US oil and increases exports, as traders can make a profit through arbitrage by selling it abroad. But that depends on shipping costs.
Rising freight rates and tight vessel availability have dimmed demand for US exports and contributed to the widening WTI-Brent spread, Georgios Sakellariou, freight analyst at Signal Maritime, said.
While the WTI-Brent spread has been trending wider in the third quarter, US crude exports have not risen significantly, according to data from ship tracker Kpler.
Shipping crude from the US Gulf Coast to Asian markets on a very large crude carrier currently costs around US$50 million in freight, according to Signal Maritime, compared with US$16 million before the Iran war broke out and drove up war risk premiums.
The discount that a barrel of US crude would need versus a European barrel to offset shipping costs was previously around minus US$4 a barrel, according to Bob Yawger, director of energy futures at Mizuho. It is now likely double that, at minus US$8, due to surging freight rates, Yawger said.
"International crude is carrying a higher scarcity and logistics premium, while US barrels are struggling to clear abroad at current transportation costs," said Shohruh Zukhritdinov, chief executive at oil trading firm NitrolOil.
The WTI-Brent spread has traded exclusively at a US$4 discount or wider since July 7, according to LSEG. Yet US crude exports have remained relatively flat month over month, rising only 45,000 barrels per day from July to August, at 3.72 million bpd, according to Kpler.
On a three-month average basis, US crude exports for September are currently on track to fall for the third consecutive month to their lowest since before the Iran war broke out in February, according to Kpler.
"A wide paper spread is an invitation to test the arbitrage, not proof that the arbitrage is open," said Zukhritdinov.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan government portal removes photos of 10 exco members
Article:
SEREMBAN: Photos of 10 Negri Sembilan executive councillors (exco) have reportedly been removed from the official state government portal.
A check of the portal at 7pm today found that only Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim's photo remained in the exco section.
According to the portal, Ismail holds three portfolios — Islamic Religious Affairs and Security; Finance, Land and Natural Resources; and Investment, Infrastructure, Utilities, Communications and Felda.
The move is believed to follow the Gazette on the Revocation of Appointment of the 10 exco members issued by the State Secretary yesterday.
The gazette, dated Sept 24, stated that the appointments of the 10 exco members were revoked with effect from Sept 20 by Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir under Article 38(5) of the Constitution of the State of Negri Sembilan 1959.
The exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
According to the gazette, all 10 took and signed their oaths and pledges of allegiance before Tuanku Muhriz on Aug 7 before assuming their positions as exco members.
"And whereas you have breached the said pledge of allegiance, therefore I hereby withdraw my assent and revoke your appointments as members of the Negri Sembilan State Executive Council," Tuanku Muhriz said in the gazette.
The gazette also stated that under Article 38(5) of the Constitution of the State of Negri Sembilan 1959, an exco member, other than the Menteri Besar, holds office at the pleasure of Tuanku Muhriz.
On Sept 20, the Negri Sembilan Palace announced that Tuanku Muhriz had revoked the appointments of all 10 exco members with immediate effect.
On Sept 16, a statement issued in the name of the State Executive Council members and published on several portals claimed that a proclamation on the election of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar under Article 11 of the Constitution of the State of Negri Sembilan 1959, dated April 19, 2026, had been signed and sealed by the legitimate Undangs and was in force.
Ismail was subsequently reported to have confirmed the proclamation concerning the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
He was reported to have said the matter had been unanimously decided by all members of the State Executive Council at a meeting the previous Tuesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Insas seeks shareholders' nod for RM530mil Inari exit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Insas Bhd, the third-largest shareholder in Inari Amertron Bhd, is seeking shareholders' approval to dispose of its entire stake in the semiconductor services company for RM529.87 million.
Inari is involved in outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing, as well as electronics manufacturing services.
The proposed sale involves 218.05 million or 5.65 per cent Inari shares, at an illustrative price of RM2.43 per share.
Insas said it has yet to identify any buyer and may sell the shares in one or more tranches through the open market or to third-party purchasers.
The proceeds would mainly be used to repay RM270 million in revolving credit facilities and fund RM248.32 million in working capital.
The repayment of the revolving credit facilities is expected to reduce the company's borrowings and save about RM13.5 million in annual interest costs.
As at Aug 31, 2026, Insas had total borrowings of RM449 million.
Based on the illustrative disposal price, Insas expects to record a net gain of about RM360 million after accounting for the shares' carrying value of RM158.32 million and estimated disposal costs.
Insas originally invested about RM23.72 million in the shares.
Inari shares closed at RM2.66 on Sept 11, giving Insas' stake a market value of about RM580 million.
The proposed disposal mandate, which is valid for 12 months, is subject to approval by Insas shareholders at a general meeting to be convened.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ETA trims stake in Indonesian canned food unit Rex Canning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ETA Group Bhd, formerly Rex Industry Bhd, is disposing of its 38 per cent stake in Indonesian canned food maker PT Rex Canning and its entire interest in dormant subsidiary Rex Foods Sdn Bhd for RM22.73 million cash.
In a bourse filing, the company said it entered into a share sale agreement with VIP Bonanza Sdn Bhd, with RM14.04 million attributable to its 38 per cent stake in Rex Canning and RM8.68 million for its 100 per cent stake in Rex Foods.
Upon completion, ETA will retain a 62 per cent stake in Rex Canning, which will remain its subsidiary.
ETA said the disposal was part of its strategy to reduce its reliance on the food and beverage (F&B) business and progressively shift its earnings mix towards property and construction.
"The board is cautiously optimistic that the financial contribution from the property and construction business will augur well with the group's future financial performance, taking into consideration the new construction contracts and awards that the group has received," it said.
The company plans to use RM22.63 million of the proceeds for general working capital, mainly for its property and construction operations, while RM100,000 will cover estimated expenses related to the disposal.
The proceeds are expected to support working capital requirements for several ongoing construction projects, including three contracts worth RM66.69 million awarded by ETA Industries Sdn Bhd on Sept 22.
Rex Canning, which manufactures and exports canned food, recorded revenue of 317.51 billion rupiah, up 25.74 per cent from the previous financial year.
Its net profit rose 368.5 per cent from a loss in the financial year ended June 30, 2024.
ETA said Rex Canning's improved performance was mainly driven by a rebound in overseas demand and better margins from higher canned food sales.
However, it noted that Rex Canning remains predominantly export-focused, with customers mainly in the United States, Europe and Asia, exposing the business to fluctuations in international demand and macroeconomic conditions.
The proposed disposal follows ETA's change in strategic direction after ETA Industries emerged as its major shareholder in June 2025.
ETA Industries completed the acquisition of 55.04 per cent of ETA's shares in July 2025.
Since then, ETA has disposed of its entire interests in Rex Canning Co Sdn Bhd and Rex Trading Sdn Bhd, which it identified as key contributors to its historical losses, and diversified into property and construction in March 2026.
The transaction is expected to result in a pro forma loss of RM100,000, subject to audit review.
The disposal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the fulfilment or waiver of conditions precedent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Favelle Favco secures RM88.8mil crane orders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Favelle Favco Bhd's unit Favelle Favco Cranes (M) Sdn Bhd has bagged three offshore crane orders worth a combined RM88.8 million.
The orders comprise the supply of offshore cranes to Saipem Offshore Construction SPA, Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Sdn Bhd and OceanMight Sdn Bhd.
Favelle Favco said the crane for Saipem Offshore Construction and the one for Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering are expected to be delivered by the end of 2027.
The crane for OceanMight is expected to be delivered by the third quarter of 2027.
The company said the contracts are expected to contribute to its earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 and beyond.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar falls as oil cools but set for weekly gain, yen rallies
Article:
HONG KONG/LONDON: The dollar fell on Friday but was on track for its second consecutive weekly gain on rising rate hike bets, while the yen rallied after Japan said Tokyo and Washington remain committed to the stance behind July's joint intervention.
The euro rose 0.2 per cent to US$1.141 as energy prices fell, moderating wagers on Federal Reserve rate increases, but was on track for a third weekly decline after touching a two-month low on Thursday.
Sterling rose 0.3 per cent to US$1.326, boosted by hawkish comments from Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. Yet it remained close to a three-month low and was set for its second straight weekly one per cent fall.
Markets have aggressively repriced the US interest rate trajectory after the Federal Reserve tightened policy last week. Robust economic data, fresh energy supply concerns and a chorus of hawkish Fed speakers have further strengthened that conviction.
A bond selloff, which sent long-dated US Treasury yields to their highest in more than 20 years, also gave the greenback a leg up.
The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, climbed to a two-month high on Thursday and was set for its first back-to-back weekly increase since June.
However, it gave back some of its recent gains and fell 0.3 per cent on Friday to 100.96.
"Whilst the dollar should get a bid from higher yields, there are still ongoing, lingering concerns around the US fiscal position, the unpredictability of US policy making," said Khoon Goh, head of Asia research at ANZ.
"I think that's why the dollar has really struggled to continue to rally, even though yields continue to increase."
Oil prices eased on Friday on signs of easing supply disruptions and hopes of progress in talks between the US and Iran. Yet crude remained close to a one-week high as a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia kept Middle East tensions high.
YEN STRENGTHENS AS JAPAN STEPS UP INTERVENTION WARNINGS
The Japanese yen bounced 0.8 per cent from three-week lows to fetch 157.65 per dollar.
The currency rose after Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said US President Donald Trump raised concern about yen weakness during a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi earlier this week.
Katayama said this reaffirmed the shared US-Japan stance behind July's joint intervention, adding she and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would stay in close contact as policymakers stepped up warnings over renewed yen weakness.
"Katayama's comment ... clearly underlines the ongoing efforts in Tokyo to portray the efforts to stem yen weakness as a continued joint strategy," said senior MUFG currency strategist Derek Halpenny.
"That certainly reinforces the possibility that additional intervention could again include the US."
Still, the yen was on track for a second weekly fall, after markets judged the Bank of Japan's rate hike last week to a 31-year high and its latest guidance as insufficiently hawkish.
Elsewhere, the offshore yuan was flat at 6.721 per dollar, as a Trump-Xi summit in Washington showed no signs of breakthroughs at a closed-door meeting on thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the Iran war.
The Australian dollar rose 0.3 per cent to US$0.703. The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to a nearly 15-year high of 4.60 per cent next week

Title: 'A significant legacy in arts and culture': Anwar pays tribute to L. Krishnan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim paid tribute to veteran film director Tan Sri Lakshmanan Krishnan, better known as L. Krishnan, who died at 104, describing him as one of the early figures who helped shape Malay cinema.
"The late L. Krishnan was a former student of Bukit Mertajam High School and among the earliest figures to shape the development of Malay cinema," he said in a social media post today.
Anwar said L. Krishnan produced important works during the 1950s and 1960s with prominent production houses, including Shaw Brothers, Malay Film Productions, Cathay-Keris and Merdeka Studios.
"Among his notable films were Bakti, Keris Sempena Riau and Selendang Merah," he said.
The prime minister also highlighted L. Krishnan's role in guiding and nurturing several prominent stars, including P. Ramlee, Maria Menado, Mustapha Maarof, M. Amin and Rosnani Jamil.
"L. Krishnan's more than 6 decades in film, advertising and music have left a significant legacy in the country's arts and cultural industry.
"His services and contributions towards enriching the nation's artistic heritage will always be remembered.
"My condolences to the entire family.
"May they be given strength and resilience in facing this loss," Anwar wrote.
The news of L. Krishnan's death was shared by
Malaysian Veteran Artistes Welfare Association
(PKAVM) president Sandakiah Azez, the daughter of late actor Datuk Aziz Sattar.

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysian Bar to challenge Najib's house arrest pardon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar will challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision and advice concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's second pardon, which allows him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
Its president Anand Raj said the Bar, through its solicitors, would challenge the decision and advice concerning the second pardon while maintaining its appeal against the board's 2024 decision to reduce Najib's prison sentence and fine.
"The Malaysian Bar will, through its solicitors, challenge the decision and advice of the Pardons Board concerning the Second Pardon, while maintaining its appeal in relation to the Pardons Board's decision and advice on the First Pardon," he said in a statement today.
The Bar also questioned the need for a public fundraiser to pay Najib's RM50 million fine, pointing out that more than RM114 million in cash seized in 2018 had been returned to his representative.
Anand said RM114,164,393.44 seized during police raids in May 2018 was returned in June 2021 after forfeiture proceedings were dismissed.
He added that jewellery, handbags and spectacles were returned to Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, while watches were returned to Najib by June 2022.
Given the assets that had been returned, Anand questioned why Umno needed to raise public funds to pay the fine.
"Such a public fundraiser may also involve other legal considerations," he said.
He also questioned reports that most of Najib's assets had been frozen, saying the returned funds appeared sufficient to cover the fine without public contributions.
"This is not clear, nor have any details been made available publicly," he said, referring to whether any other unseized assets remained frozen.
On the legal effect of a pardon, Anand said it did not amount to an exoneration of guilt.
"Neither a pardon, a reprieve, nor a respite constitutes an exoneration of guilt or removal of wrongdoing. They do not 'wipe the slate clean' of the prior conviction," he said.
He also cited High Court judge Alice Loke's ruling last December that Malaysian law makes no provision for house arrest, a position he said had previously been confirmed by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
"From our research to date, there appear to be no standard operating procedures or guidelines in place for 'house arrests'.
"A whole new ecosystem of rules and procedures would be required to operationalise 'house arrests'," he said.
The Bar called on the Pardons Board and the Prime Minister's Department to declassify and publish the minutes of the board's meetings concerning both of Najib's pardons.
It also called for full disclosure of the conditions of the house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and additional costs to taxpayers.
Citing a joint statement issued by civil society groups and individuals, including Datuk Ambiga Sreenevasan and Maria Chin Abdullah, the Bar renewed its call for a freedom of information framework to ensure public access to such details.
Anand also raised concerns about the precedent that the decision could set.
"The Pardons Board will now receive many more petitions for 'house arrest'.
"Clear and objective criteria, made known in advance, are crucial to avoid any perceptions of preferential treatment for Najib.
"On what basis may any
other convict or prisoner seek a similar pardon,
reprieve or respite?" he said.
On Sept 18, the Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.
Najib, 73, was convicted in 2020 of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million from SRC International. He was initially sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his prison sentence to 6 years and his fine to RM50 million.
He is also seeking a stay of execution of a separate 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.

Title: Nancy urges women to be bold, lead with clear vision
Article:
KUCHING: Women need the courage to step forward to lead and set a clear direction to play a greater role in shaping society, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said leadership is not merely about politics or holding key positions, but about helping communities and meeting others' needs.
"Politics is about taking care of others and their needs… so that must be in your plans, how you see yourself helping others.
"Leaders must also possess high empathy and align their leadership spirit with actions to benefit the community," she said at the opening of the Apprentice Programme: Dayak Women and Grassroots Leadership in Governance, Decision-Making and Sustainable Development here today.
Nancy also reminded leaders to be astute in facing challenges, remain calm when resolving problems and know when to speak up.
"A leader does not necessarily need to speak a lot, as there are times when one needs to remain silent and listen to learn something.
"Every individual holding a leadership position must ensure tangible achievements that give back to society, or provide a return on investment (ROI), from their responsibilities," she said.
She described the success of Dr Florence Christie, who represented Sarawak at the Global Alliance for Healthy Cities (AFHC) 2026 Conference in Sydney, Australia, as proof that Sarawakian women can step onto the international stage. - BERNAMA

Title: Three Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings at 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today, down from four at 2pm after Sri Aman improved to the moderate category.
Serian recorded the highest reading at 169, down from 174 at 2pm.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System, Samarahan recorded 156, down from 161, while Kuching eased to 154 from 162.
Sri Aman recorded 98, the highest reading in the moderate category, after registering 156 at 2pm.
Elsewhere, Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded a reading of 91, followed by Larkin and Pasir Gudang in Johor at 85 each and Nilai in Negri Sembilan at 83.
Readings in other parts of Sarawak also improved, with Bintulu and Sarikei recording 81 each and Kapit 77.
In the Klang Valley, Shah Alam recorded 80 and Johan Setia 78, both in the moderate category.
Three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah in Kelantan at 49, Langkawi in Kedah at 40 and Besut in Terengganu at 32.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate and 101 to 200 unhealthy.
Haze conditions were reported to have improved this morning, with only
four areas in Sarawak
recording unhealthy readings as of 8am.

Title: Zahid applauds national heroes after historic sepak takraw gold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated the national men's sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
In a Facebook post, he said the success ended Malaysia's 36-year wait to reclaim gold in the event.
"Alhamdulillah, after a 36-year wait, the gold medal finally belongs to Malaysia once again. My congratulations to the national men's sepak takraw squad for their proud achievement in the team regu event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
"Another historic moment has been created. Well done, national heroes! Continue to make Malaysia proud on the world stage," he said.
Earlier, the national sepak takraw squad clinched the men's team regu gold medal after defeating Thailand 2-0 in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Arena.
The victory emulated the feat achieved at the 1990 Asian Games in Beijing and gave Malaysia its fourth gold medal of the games. - BERNAMA

Title: Malaysia among 'fabulous five' Asean economies set to attract more FDI – Economist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is among five Asean economies poised to attract more foreign direct investment (FDI), supported by their strengths in manufacturing and digital infrastructure.
Juwai IQI global chief economist Shan Saeed said the five economies — Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Vietnam — are well placed to benefit as investment shifts towards productive capacity in the region.
"Asean's investment centre of gravity is shifting towards productive capacity — and five economies are underwriting that transition," he told Bernama in a statement.
Shan, who calls the group the "Fabulous Five", estimated that they received US$85.3 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in FDI in 2025, or about 35 per cent of Asean's US$243.9 billion total. His estimate was based on data in the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development's World Investment Report 2026.
He also estimated that the five economies accounted for US$84.8 billion, or about 80 per cent, of Asean's US$105.6 billion in announced greenfield investment.
"The pipeline is the more telling signal. These projects represent investment intentions rather than disbursed capital, but their concentration indicates where the region's next factories, data centres and semiconductor capacity are likely to emerge," he said.
Citing the Asean Investment Report 2025, he said that manufacturing FDI in the region rose nearly 150 per cent to US$44 billion in 2024.
"Digital infrastructure strengthens the thesis," he said, pointing to McKinsey's estimate that the global data centre value chain would require about US$6.7 trillion in cumulative investment between 2025 and 2030.
He noted that McKinsey identified Johor, alongside Jakarta in Indonesia and Chonburi in Thailand, to be among Asia's emerging data centre locations.
Shan also cited The Economist's discussion of whether Malaysia's data centre expansion could help the country move beyond middle-income status.
He said the five economies offer complementary strengths: Indonesia's resources, Malaysia's semiconductor and digital infrastructure sectors, Thailand's manufacturing capacity, Vietnam's export platform and the Philippines' services sector.
However, he said that conversion, not attraction, is the harder test.
"Energy security, regulatory credibility and human-capital depth will determine how much announced investment becomes operating capacity -- and how effectively that capacity generates technology transfer, skilled employment and higher-value supply chains.
"Scale attracts capital. Credibility converts it. Execution compounds it," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar congratulates sepak takraw squad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the national men's sepak takraw team after they ended a 36-year wait for the Asian Games team regu gold medal in Aichi-Nagoya today.
Anwar described the victory as a significant and proud moment for Malaysians after the national team defeated traditional rivals Thailand 2-0 in the final at Nagoya City Mizuho Arena.
"Congratulations to the national sepak takraw squad on ending a 36-year wait to win gold again in the men's team regu event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026," he said in a social media post.
The gold was Malaysia's fourth at the Games and provided a boost to the national contingent as competition continues in Aichi-Nagoya.
"This success also delivered the fourth gold medal for the Malaysian contingent at the Games, making it a very meaningful victory that makes all Malaysians proud," he said.
The victory was particularly significant for the sepak takraw team, who last won the team regu gold at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, when they also defeated Thailand in the final.
Anwar also urged the national athletes to continue fighting and flying the Malaysian flag on the international stage.
"Congratulations, Malaysian children. Continue to make the country proud!" he said.

Title: Orang Asli woman missing after fishing trip in Rompin
Article:
ROMPIN: An Orang Asli woman has been reported missing after she failed to return home from a fishing trip near Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, here on Sept 22.
Kuang Poh, 73, from Kampung Api Larat in Pekan, was last seen leaving her home for the swampy area near Kampung Lesung about 3pm.
Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said a relative lodged a police report at about 5pm on Sept 23 after being alerted by a family member.
He said the search and rescue operation began yesterday, involving more than 30 personnel from the Fire and Rescue Department, Wildlife and National Parks Department, police and villagers.
"They searched along a logging road through the forest towards Sungai Rompin. Due to the risk of encounters with wild animals, the search operation ended about 6pm when it became dark.
"The search operation resumed today with the assistance of two tracker dogs. The search radius covers about 5km from the missing woman's house," he said in a statement today.
Sharif Shai said an operations centre had been set up at Kampung Lesung to coordinate the search.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Inspector Mohammad Nazir Hanapi at 017-9883784 or the nearest police station.

Title: Singapore population hits 6.21 million as non-resident numbers climb
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's total population rose 1.6 per cent year-on-year to 6.21 million as of June 2026, from 6.11 million a year earlier, according to the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD).
In its Population In Brief 2026 report released on Friday, NPTD said the citizen population increased by 0.7 per cent to 3.68 million in June 2026 from 3.66 million in the previous year, while the permanent resident population remained relatively stable at 0.55 million.
"The non-resident population stood at 1.98 million in June 2026, an increase of 3.7 per cent from June 2025," it said.
The report indicated that the population increase was mainly attributable to growth in the non-resident population, particularly the rising number of work permit holders in the construction sector.
The increase in work permit holders was to support key projects such as Changi Terminal 5, the Marina Bay Sands expansion and the ramp-up of housing supply and transport infrastructure, it said.
Meanwhile, NPTD highlighted that 26,071 citizen births were recorded in 2025, down 10.8 per cent from 29,237 in 2024.
Additionally, 21,671 citizen marriages were registered in 2025, down 5.6 per cent from 22,955 in 2024.
The resident total fertility rate (TFR) was 0.87 in 2025, down from 0.97 in 2024, it said. - BERNAMA

Title: SkyWorld on track for RM4.6bil GDV target
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SkyWorld Development Bhd says it is on track to achieve RM4.6 billion in cumulative post-listing gross development value (GDV) launches by the end of 2026.
This will be supported by new launches targeted for the year, totalling more than RM2.0 billion.
Chief executive officer Lee Chee Seng said the property developer has RM1.1 billion in unbilled sales, which provides earnings visibility as it works to strengthen its financial performance.
"Timely delivery remains fundamental to our long-term growth and we are strengthening our execution capabilities by deploying prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) technology in Penang by the end of the financial year (FY27)," he said in a statement following the company's annual general meeting today.
Beyond Malaysia, Lee said SkySolis Residences in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam marked an important milestone in the group's regional expansion.
The initiatives are part of SkyWorld 2040, the company's 15-year long-term strategic plan aimed at driving its next phase of growth, transformation and sustainable urban development.
Founder and non-independent executive chairman Datuk Seri Ng Thien Phing said SkyWorld remained committed to urban affordable housing, where demand continued to outpace supply.
He said the company aimed to evolve from a Malaysia-based city developer into one of Southeast Asia's top 30 property developers, while targeting cumulative profit after tax of RM1.0 billion for FY27-31.
Meanwhile, shareholders at today's AGM approved all ordinary resolutions tabled.
This included the re-election of directors and reappointment of Deloitte PLT as external auditor for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.
Shareholders also received the audited financial statements for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, together with the directors' and auditors' reports.

Title: China leaves business leaders at home as Xi courts Trump in Washington
Article:
BEIJING: Chinese business executives were notably absent during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington, a stark contrast to the titans of US business turning out for a black-tie dinner at the White House.
Of the 134 names on the guest list for Thursday's extravagant White House state banquet, only 19 were part of the Chinese delegation leaving experts divided over the motivation behind the obvious imbalance.
"I would say it simply reflects the reality that Xi and China's priority is not business or trade deals, but to make the visit a success, at least in terms of optics," Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute said.
"If trade were very high priority, they would have senior business leaders on tow."
Apart from Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan, the Chinese delegation included his right-hand man Cai Qi, the country's top diplomat Wang Yi and Chinese ambassador to the United States and top trade negotiator He Lifeng.
Those joining the high-profile evening for the US included Apple's Tim Cook, Lisa Su of memory chip giant Advanced Micro Devices and Jensen Huang of Nvidia – which has been banned from exporting its best semiconductors to China.
Tech icons Mark Zuckerberg, Open AI's Sam Altman and Jeff Bezos were also invited, as was Elon Musk.
The Chinese foreign ministry refused to comment when asked by reporters whether a trade delegation would travel with Xi.
Experts also raised the sensitive way Chinese business activities are viewed in the US, to internal Chinese bureaucracy, visa issues, or a deliberate move by Beijing among possible reasons.
"I understand originally the Chinese government did want to bring some Chinese CEOs to join Xi for the state visit," said George Chen, Chair of Digital Practice at The Asia Group.
"But such a plan fell apart mainly due to internal bureaucracy and process problems such as visas for some Chinese CEOs, as their companies are in sensitive sectors like AI, semiconductors and batteries."
"Xi is also pragmatic in economic affairs," added Dan Wang, of the Eurasia Group. "Neither side could make strategic concessions on tech, China is set to be more self-sufficient in tech without increasing reliance on US chips."
"The point of bringing Chinese tech or state-owned enterprise CEOs to the US also seems pointless given the political pushback in Congress," she told AFP.
In contrast Trump intended to "show off American tech and AI, and he succeeded", Jean-Pierre Cabestan, from the Hong Kong Baptist University said.
- 'SUPPORTING ROLE' -
When Xi visited the United States as president in 2015, there were 15 Chinese businesspeople – including Alibaba's Jack Ma – among the delegation, according to state media.
On a 2012 trip as vice president Xi led a delegation of 500 entrepreneurs.
But the longer Xi has remained in office, the more unlikely it has become for him to bring a business delegation on trips abroad.
In April 2014, President Xi visited four European countries – the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Belgium – with an accompanying economic and trade delegation of over 200 entrepreneurs.
His state visit to Britain in 2015 was accompanied by 150 business people.
On his 2024 trip to France Xi was accompanied by "a delegation of Chinese entrepreneurs", from both state-owned and private enterprises, but official sources did not list an exact number.
Meanwhile visits this year to Egypt, Kyrgyzstan and Pyongyang don't detail any trade delegation at all accompanying the president – nor on a high-profile state visit to Russia last year.
However, Chen said the lack of a trade delegation did not mean that the visit would not be beneficial for Chinese businesses.
"China is all about the government, top-down decision making, and the Chinese private sector has little influence or leverage on the government – unlike how much lobbying power Elon Musk, Tim Cook and others may have on President Trump," he said.
"China CEOs always play the supporting role and the two lead actors this week are Xi and Trump. As long as the two leaders had good meetings...that's good for both Chinese and American business for the long term."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two tahfiz students charged with injuring schoolmate with iron
Article:
PARIT: Two tahfiz school students, aged 13 and 14, were charged in the magistrate's court here today with injuring a fellow student with an iron.
They pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Nurul Izalina Rajaai in closed-door proceedings.
The pair were jointly charged with intentionally causing hurt to a 13-year-old student using an iron, a weapon likely to cause death, at a tahfiz school here.
The incident allegedly occurred about 4pm on Sept 19.
The charge was framed under Section 324 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which carries a maximum 10-year jail term, a fine, whipping, or any two of these punishments upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor R. Jayasri prosecuted, while the two students were represented by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Nur Nadrah Badarudin.
The court allowed bail of RM500 each and fixed Oct 27 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit closes higher against US dollar despite Fed rate hike expectations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar on Friday, driven by bargain-hunting activity despite expectations of further US interest rate hikes.
At 6pm, the ringgit increased to 4.0715/0765 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0840/0880.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit strengthened to RM4.0673 against the US dollar early in the morning before giving up some of its gains to trade at RM4.0743 in the afternoon.
He said the US Dollar Index (DXY) remained well supported at 101.182 points as the odds of the Federal Reserve (Fed) raising interest rates stayed high.
"Based on the interest rate futures contract, the odds of rate hikes in October and December currently stand at 70.9 per cent and 80.6 per cent, respectively, up from 55.4 per cent and 77.6 per cent last Monday," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It gained against the euro to 4.6378/6435 from 4.6451/6497 at Thursday's close and advanced vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3907/3973 from 5.4023/4076. However, it eased versus the Japanese yen to 2.5764/5797 from 2.5723/5750 previously.
The local note traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It strengthened versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1858/1900 from 3.1906/1940 at Thursday's close and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.4/227.8 from 227.9/228.2.
However, the ringgit weakened versus the Thai baht to 12.2036/2234 from 12.1950/2121 yesterday and slipped vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.52/6.53 from 6.51/6.52.

Title: SUV driver held after fatal crash with motorcyclist in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: Police have detained the driver of a sports utility vehicle (SUV) after his vehicle allegedly crashed into an oncoming motorcyclist, killing the rider near a petrol station along Jalan Semambu here today.
Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the 56-year-old motorcyclist, who was travelling alone, was killed in the 8am crash.
"The accident involved an SUV and a motorcycle. The 29-year-old SUV driver is believed to have lost control of his vehicle before veering into the opposite lane and crashing into the oncoming motorcycle.
"Police have obtained the dashcam footage and will conduct inspections on the vehicles involved, as well as other tests, as part of the investigation," he said in a statement.
Ashari said the motorcyclist suffered severe injuries and died at the scene. He said the victim's remains were taken to Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital for a post-mortem.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years, a fine of up to RM50,000 and a driving disqualification of at least five years.

Title: Johari: Corruption risks must be spotted early, not addressed later
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Integrity units in every organisation must to be empowered as strategic partners to top management in identifying corruption risks at an early stage, rather than merely handling complaints or follow-up action after violations occur.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the units should also play a role in addressing systemic weaknesses and fostering a culture of integrity within organisations.
He said corruption prevention must begin before a case occurs through good governance, effective control systems, education, workplace culture and values instilled in every individual.
"Integrity units should not be seen merely as units that handle complaints or compliance after a violation has occurred.
"Instead, they need to become strategic partners to management in identifying risks early, addressing systemic weaknesses and building a culture of integrity within organisations," he said in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Fifth National Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption 2026 here.
Johari said the success of the units should not be measured solely by the number of cases uncovered, but by their ability to identify risks early, address systemic weaknesses and make a culture of integrity part of an organisation's DNA.
He said when institutions are strengthened, good governance is implemented and integrity becomes part of an organisation's culture, opportunities for corruption can be reduced.
"I believe that when Integrity Units are empowered, management provides the necessary support and research findings are utilised in decision-making, we will have a much stronger corruption prevention ecosystem," he said.
Johari also said efforts to combat corruption must not be merely reactive, adding that prevention should begin by identifying systemic weaknesses, strengthening governance and building a culture of integrity in every organisation.
He said the success of the anti-corruption agenda should also not be measured solely by the number of arrests, charges or convictions.
"The broader measure is whether we have succeeded in closing avenues for corruption, addressing weaknesses in the system and building an organisational culture that truly upholds integrity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuching Marathon cancellation a blow to 13,000 participants who made travel plans, says Sarawak sports minister
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — Sarawak Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah has expressed disappointment over the last-minute cancellation of Kuching Marathon 2026, which had attracted more than 13,000 registered participants.
He said the decision was particularly difficult for participants from outside Sarawak who had made advance arrangements, including booking flights and accommodation.
“If it is indeed cancelled, I myself feel sad because of the hopes of those who came and registered. We also know that there are more than 13,000 participants.
“Many of them came from outside Sarawak and had already booked accommodation such as hotels and homestays. Some travelled by plane, which involved costs to attend the marathon,” he said when commenting on the cancellation.
Earlier today, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) announced that the event, scheduled for Sunday (Sept 27), had been cancelled due to the prevailing haze affecting Kuching and surrounding areas.
Abdul Karim said he had been at the race pack collection venue shortly before the announcement and had not been informed about the cancellation at the time.
However, he said he understood that the organisers would have had valid reasons for making the decision, possibly following advice from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC).
“I believe the organisers must have had certain reasons for cancelling it, possibly on the advice of PDRM and SDMC,” he said.
Abdul Karim said his ministry had also provided financial assistance towards the organisation of the event, although its implementation remained subject to various considerations.
He said he understood if the cancellation prompted criticism from participants, particularly those who had already made travel and accommodation arrangements.
At the same time, some participants had praised the organisers for prioritising public health and safety despite the decision coming shortly before the event.
Meanwhile, KMA said registered participants could collect their finisher medals and finisher tees tomorrow (Sept 26) and Sunday at the Alfresco area of Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre.
Collection will be available from 9am to 9pm tomorrow and from 8am to 1pm on Sunday.
Participants must present their physical race bib at the designated category counter to collect their finisher medal and, where applicable, finisher tee.
One person may collect the items on behalf of up to five participants, provided the physical race bibs of each participant are presented.
Participants who have yet to collect their race packs must do so before collecting their finisher medal and finisher tee.
Race pack collection will remain open on Sunday from 10am to noon. — The Borneo Post

Title: EC: 43,309 new voters added in August — check the electoral roll by October 24
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for August 2026 (DPT BLN8/2026) is open for review for 30 days until Oct 24, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus.
He said DPT BLN8/2026, which was gazetted yesterday, contains the names of 43,309 citizens aged 18 and above during the period from Aug 1 to 31, 2026, who were automatically registered as new electors.
Khairul Shahril said it also includes 34,411registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies and 2,728 voters who have changed their voter category or status.
He urged voters in the relevant categories to check their names in the DPT BLN8/2026.
“Checks can be made via the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the official state election office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my, the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak mobile application, or the Voter Registration Check hotline at 03-8892 7218,” he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril said those who find that their names are not listed in the DPT BLN8/2026 may submit a claim by completing Form C through the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my or by visiting the relevant State Election Office.
Any registered voter in an electoral constituency who, after checking the roll, wishes to object to the inclusion of the name of a voter who has transferred into the constituency may do so by completing Form D through the same channels.
Forms C and D can also be downloaded from the State Election Office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my and submitted to the relevant state election director, together with the objection fee, during office hours throughout the DPT BLN8/2026 review period. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s Asian Games sepak takraw gold after 36-year wait
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the national men’s sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
He described their success in ending the country’s 36-year wait to reclaim the gold medal, which was also Malaysia’s fourth gold at Asiad 2026, as a highly meaningful victory and a source of pride for all Malaysians.
“
Syabas
(Well done) Malaysia. Continue to bring glory to Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, the national sepak takraw squad clinched the men’s team regu gold medal after defeating Thailand 2-0 in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Arena.
Malaysia last won gold in the event when they defeated the same opponents at the 1990 edition in Beijing. — Bernama

Title: Immigration detains 84 foreign nationals in two-phase raid at Putrajaya’s ‘Green Flats’
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department detained 84 foreign nationals under Ops Pintu at Pangsapuri Putra Harmoni, better known as the “Green Flats”, here following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs.
It said 60 Immigration personnel conducted the operation in two phases beginning yesterday.
“The first phase of the operation began at 11.30am yesterday, with business premises in the apartment area inspected and enforcement action taken.
“The operation resumed at 1.3 am today, with residents suspected of being illegal immigrants as the main target,” it said in a statement today.
It said 321 people were inspected, while 84 foreign nationals — 73 men, nine women and two children — were detained for further investigation.
“Intelligence gathering revealed the presence of foreign nationals residing in the area, with some believed to be conducting business activities there,” it said, adding that Ops Pintu was a continuation of enforcement operations in settlements identified as having a high density of foreign nationals, following an operation conducted on September 9.
As such, the department urged owners of houses and premises to be responsible for their tenants and ensure that the immigration status of occupants or tenants is valid and complies with the stipulated requirements.
“At the same time, the public is encouraged to continue providing information regarding the presence of illegal immigrants or activities suspected of violating the law,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Bar seeks disclosure of taxpayer cost of Najib house arrest, plans fresh court challenge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Malaysian government should disclose the additional cost to taxpayers if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak serves the remainder of his SRC International jail term under house arrest, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj said today.
In a statement, Anand urged the Federal Territories Pardons Board and the Prime Minister’s Department to disclose two things to the public:
“Declassify and publish the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting(s) held regarding Najib’s First Pardon and Najib’s Second Pardon decisions”; and
“Fully disclose all conditions proposed to be attached to Najib’s house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and the additional costs to taxpayers that a ‘house arrest’ would entail.”
In calling for greater transparency, Anand said the Malaysian Bar had adopted a joint statement issued on September 22 by 37 civil society groups and 387 individuals, including former Bersih leaders Datuk Ambiga Sreenevasan and Maria Chin Abdullah, as well as Martabat PJ.
The joint statement urged the Pardons Board to release the full minutes and recorded justifications for its decision-making process in relation to Najib’s two pardons, under which his SRC sentence was first reduced and he was subsequently allowed to serve the remainder under house arrest if he fulfils certain conditions.
Anand also announced today that the Malaysian Bar would go to court to challenge the Pardons Board’s decision and advice concerning Najib’s second pardon.
“The Malaysian Bar will, through its solicitors, challenge the decision and advice of the Pardons Board concerning the Second Pardon, while maintaining its appeal in relation to the Pardons Board’s decision and advice on the First Pardon,” he said.
Najib has been imprisoned since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
The first pardon referred to by Anand was the January 2024 decision that reduced Najib’s 12-year jail term to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
The second, granted on September 18, allows Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided he pays the RM50 million fine and complies with other conditions.
Najib remains in prison as he has yet to pay the RM50 million fine.
His lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said today that Najib could not afford to pay the fine, noting that his bank accounts remain frozen.
Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj has called for the full conditions and taxpayer costs of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest to be disclosed, as the Bar prepares a fresh legal challenge over the former prime minister’s second pardon. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
About ‘house arrest’ in Malaysia
Among other things, Anand noted that then High Court judge Alice Loke had ruled in a court case involving Najib that Malaysia has no legal mechanism for house arrest.
He said the home minister had also confirmed that there was no law providing for house arrest, while the Cabinet had approved in principle the drafting and tabling of legislation on house arrest.
Addressing claims involving the purported house arrest of Kenneth Lee Fook Mun, a grandson of Tun H.S. Lee, Anand said the case was not a “legal precedent for granting house arrest” or legal authority for the proposition that Malaysia has a formal house-arrest framework.
Anand said Lee’s case did not appear to have been tested or endorsed by a court, and that it remained unclear whether his purported house arrest arose from a Pardons Board decision or from a release on licence by the Commissioner General of Prisons under Section 43 of the Prison Act 1995.
“Finally, from our research to date, there appear to be no standard operating procedures or guidelines in place for ‘house arrests’. A whole new ecosystem of rules and procedures would be required to operationalise ‘house arrests’,” he said.
Status of Malaysian Bar’s existing court challenge to Najib’s first pardon
On April 26, 2024, the Malaysian Bar filed a court challenge against Najib’s first pardon, which reduced his SRC sentence.
In that case, the Malaysian Bar sought to challenge the validity of the Pardons Board’s 2024 decision and advice.
It also sought a court order prohibiting the Pardons Board from considering any further pardon for Najib “until all criminal proceedings against him have been exhausted, and until he has publicly accepted responsibility for his actions and expressed repentance and remorse”.
As the challenge was brought through judicial review, the Malaysian Bar first had to obtain the court’s leave to proceed with the case.
The High Court on November 11, 2024, refused leave for the Malaysian Bar to proceed with the challenge.
The Court of Appeal is scheduled to deliver its decision on January 7, 2027, on the Malaysian Bar’s appeal against the High Court ruling.
