Title: EC denies report of 15 new parliamentary seats for Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) has denied a report claiming that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased, saying there is currently no proposal to alter the number of federal seats in the state.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said no documents had been shared indicating that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased to any particular number.
“The EC wishes to emphasise that there is currently no proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies involving areas in Sarawak, as alleged by the newspaper to involve discussions related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63),” he said in a statement.
Khairul Shahril said the only redelineation exercise currently being undertaken by the EC was the Seventh Sarawak Electoral Constituency Redelineation Review, with its proposals being displayed for public inspection from September 1 to 30.
The review proposes 17 new state constituencies, increasing the number of Sarawak Legislative Assembly seats from 82 to 99, as well as changes to the names of several existing state constituencies and one parliamentary constituency.
He urged the public to refer only to verified information on the redelineation exercise through the EC’s official portal and statements issued by the commission.
The denial follows a Berita Harian report earlier today claiming Sarawak could see 15 new parliamentary constituencies under a proposed electoral redelineation exercise, which would increase the state’s representation in the Dewan Rakyat from 31 to 46 seats.
The report said the proposal was aimed at moving Sabah and Sarawak’s combined parliamentary representation towards one-third of the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the MA63. — The Borneo Post

Title: MACC completes Kedah fertiliser probe, two may face charges soon
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed its investigation into the delayed supply of fertilisers in Kedah, with two individuals set to be charged soon in connection with the case.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the charges will be brought under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009, which pertains to misappropriation and false documents.
“The MACC investigation into the issue of fertiliser distribution to farmers and paddy planters in Kedah has been completed.
“We will refer the case to the Attorney General, and if consent is granted regarding our recommendation, the charges will likely be registered in court next week or the week after,” he told a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 5th National Governance, Integrity, and Anti-Corruption Research Conference 2026 here today.
Abd Halim, however, did not reveal the identities of the individuals to be charged.
On September 7, the MACC opened an investigation paper into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser, or Paddy Fertiliser 3, to Kedah paddy farmers. The investigation followed a complaint lodged by the Malaysian Paddy Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (PeSAWAH) on August 26.
The delay by the supplier appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) affected paddy farmers across a 100,000-hectare area under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA). — Bernama

Title: MACC chief: Two former Felda officials to be charged over Kuala Lumpur Vertical City project next week
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — Two individuals being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project linked to Felda will be charged next week, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said.
He said the two were a former Felda general manager and a former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee, also known as Felda Investment Commission.
"The Attorney General has given consent to charge the two individuals involved. The former Felda general manager will face one charge under Section 420, and the charge will be registered in court on September 30.
"The other individual, the former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee or Commission, will face two charges under Section 417, and the charges will be brought on September 29," he told a press conference after the Fifth National Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference closing ceremony here today.
The KLVC investigation is among seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.
The investigations focus on asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020, which are suspected to involve elements of corruption, misappropriation and abuse of power. — Bernama

Title: More questioning awaits Isa Samad in Felda probe once he recovers from eye surgery, says MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will resume recording the statement of Datuk Seri Isa Samad once the former Felda chairman recovers from a medical procedure.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa is being treated at the Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery.
“Regarding Isa’s statement, we had to put it on hold. It was supposed to be recorded yesterday and today, but since he is unwell, we have postponed it until we receive information on his health status from the Prisons Department.
“Once he has recovered, we will continue recording his statement. There is still a lot that needs to be recorded from him,” he told a press conference after the closing ceremony for the 5th National Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference here today.
Earlier, the media reported that the MACC confirmed it recorded Isa’s statement at the Sungai Buloh Prison on September 17 to assist in investigations into the Op Fella case.
Abdul Halim said the statement was recorded in connection with Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FICSB)’s purchase and investment of assets, which are suspected to involve elements of corruption and misappropriation. — Bernama

Title: Witness tails fleeing hatchback after attempted theft, helping police make arrest in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — A witness who followed a hatchback believed to have been used by two men fleeing an attempted vehicle component theft helped police trace their movements and arrest one suspect here last night.
Padawan district police chief Supt Barry William said the incident occurred at about 8.40am yesterday at a workshop along Jalan Batu Kawa here.
He said the witness spotted two men allegedly attempting to steal components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop.
“A witness noticed two suspicious men trying to steal the components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop before they fled using the hatchback after being confronted.
“The witness, who is the driver of a four-wheel drive (4WD) managed to track down and tail the hatchback, thus helping police trace the suspects’ movements,” he said in a statement.
The hatchback was later found abandoned in Jalan Rantau Panjang.
Police subsequently arrested one of the suspects, a 25-year-old man, at about 9.15pm the same day.
A metal box and car key were also seized to assist investigations.
Police are continuing efforts to track down the other suspect or suspects believed to be involved.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 read with Section 511 of the Penal Code for attempted theft. — The Borneo Post

Title: MACC to issue asset declaration notices to Saravanan, his wife and three children
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will issue notices to former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan, his wife, and their three children to declare their assets within a month.
Its chief commissioner, Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, said that the asset declaration notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009 will be delivered on Monday to Saravanan, his wife, and their two children, while another child who is still abroad will receive it in November.
“They have been informed and will attend the MACC headquarters for the delivery of the notices.
“A period of 30 days (for asset declaration) is given, and if that period is insufficient, an extension will be granted if they apply,” he said at a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 5th National Level Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption 2026, here today.
Saravanan was previously charged in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court with three counts of receiving bribes amounting to nearly RM1.09 million related to the approval of 1,000 foreign worker quotas for a company, four years ago.
In another development, Abd Halim said his side has not yet received the asset declaration from the former chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, and his family.
“We just submitted the notices on Sept 15. Wait for a month,” he said.
The MACC served asset declaration notices on Abdul Azeez and his family under Section 49 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorism Financing Act 2001. — Bernama

Title: Perak court fines buyer, petrol station owner RM25,000 each over RON95 sale to Singapore car
Article:
MANJUNG, Sept 25 — An oil palm plantation worker and a petrol station owner were each fined RM25,000 by the Sessions Court here today for their involvement in buying and selling RON95 petrol for foreign-registered vehicles.
Judge Azizah Ahmad handed down the sentence against Wong Ing Wan, 46, and Ling Mei Yen, 51, after they pleaded guilty to the charges and also sentenced them to two months in prison if they failed to pay the fine. Both paid the fine.
Wong was charged with violating Regulation 4(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for purchasing 27.452 litres of RON95 petrol for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.
He was accused of committing the act at the Siew Service Station in Ayer Tawar at 8:25pm on May 13 under Regulation 4(3) of the same Regulations, punishable under Section 22(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, which carries a fine not exceeding RM1 million, a maximum prison term of three years, or both for a first offence.
Meanwhile, Ling was charged — at the same date, time, and location — with violating Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for selling the same petrol to Wong for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.
The charge was filed under Regulation 3(2) of the similar Regulations, punishable under Section 22(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, which provides for the same penalty.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Nazreen Zabarudin requested the court to impose a proportionate sentence on the two unrepresented accused, taking into account public interest and the fact that the case involved the controlled substance RON95.
He added that the offence involving the sale and purchase of petrol using the BUDI Madani quota had also gone viral and drawn public condemnation.
Wong and Ling pleaded for a lenient sentence as it was their first offence. The man noted he supports his wife, a child, and an elderly mother, while the woman cares for her 80-year-old father and three children who are still studying. — Bernama

Title: When will Melaka vote? EC to decide key state election dates on October 7
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on October 7 to discuss matters related to the 16th Melaka state election.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting followed the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly last Wednesday.
“The special meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.
“Matters to be discussed include key dates for the 16th Melaka state election, including the writ of election, nomination day, polling day, the electoral roll to be used, and other preparations for the election,” he said in a statement today.
He said a press conference would be held immediately after the meeting.
Last Tuesday, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the State Assembly effective Wednesday, after obtaining the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam. — Bernama

Title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas.
In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze.
It said the decision was made after consultation with relevant authorities and medical advisers, with the health and safety of participants, crew members, volunteers, officials, medical teams, and the public taking precedence.
“To honour the commitment of our runners, all registered participants may collect their finisher medal and finisher tee starting tomorrow at Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre (Alfresco Area),” KMA said in a statement.
It added that detailed collection schedules and instructions would be announced on its official social media platforms.
The cancellation came shortly after State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah visited the Kuching Marathon registration and race pack collection at Plaza Merdeka.
Map shows the route for what would have been the 42km full marathon. — Picture from Facebook/Kuching Marathon via The Borneo Post
When met by reporters, Abdul Karim had said the decision on whether the marathon could proceed would depend on the prevailing haze situation and assessments by the relevant authorities.
Abdul Karim, who is also State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister, said the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) had established indicators based on API readings to determine whether outdoor events could be safely held.
“I’m not in the capacity to say yes or no for the race to be conducted, because we in Sarawak do have the SDMC to determine whether an outdoor event should be held or not,” he said.
He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.
The first Kuching Marathon was held on August 17, 2014, and has since grown into one of Borneo’s largest international mass-participation running events.
Participation grew rapidly, surpassing 10,000 runners by 2019, with subsequent editions attracting participants from more than 40 countries. — The Borneo Post

Title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today.
The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.
“Initial police investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred when the Honda Jazz driven by the victim, travelling from Kulai Besar towards Johor Bahru, lost control.
“The woman’s car then crashed into the rear of a lorry driven by a 66-year-old local man who was stopped at a traffic light,” he said in a statement.
Tan said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Fatin Mohd Radzi at 018-3649199.

Title: PM’s brother Idrus Ibrahim buried in Bukit Mertajam after Friday prayers
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The remains of Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, were laid to rest at the Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Muslim Cemetery here today.
The funeral was attended by hundreds of family members, relatives, friends and political leaders from various parties.
Earlier, the remains were taken from the family home at 12.20 pm in a van to the temporary prayer hall at Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Jamek Mosque on Jalan Kolam.
The prime minister, accompanied by family members and members of the public, walked about 200 metres from the late Idrus’ home to the prayer hall.
The funeral prayers, held after Friday prayers, were led by Penang Mufti Assoc Prof Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman. The remains were then taken to the cemetery and buried at 2.10 pm.
Penang Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah paid their respects to the late Idrus at the family home at 11.15 am.
Also present to pay their last respects were Penang Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid; Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister and Bukit Mertajam MP Steven Sim; and political leaders from various parties.
Idrus died in his sleep at his residence at 6.10 pm yesterday. He was 83.
The former teacher is survived by his wife, four children and 10 grandchildren. — Bernama

Title: Vulnerable groups to be focus of Selangor Budget 2027, says MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Supporting vulnerable groups will be among the Selangor government’s main priorities in Budget 2027, with the aim of ensuring the state’s economic progress benefits people across all segments of society.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor’s development should go beyond strong economic performance and attracting investment to also addressing the needs of groups requiring greater attention, according to a
Berita Harian
report published today.
“We want to ensure that this state is not only developed with a good economy, that we are not only able to attract high investment, and that we can remain the ‘heartbeat of Malaysian economy’ or serve as an example in developing the artificial intelligence (AI), micro-business, microchip or semiconductor sectors.
“Instead, we need to look at specific groups that require attention so that the state’s economic progress and development are enjoyed fairly by the people of this state,” he said.
Amirudin said existing support programmes, including cash handouts and assistance under Bantuan Kehidupan Sejahtera Selangor (Bingkas) and YANIS, would be part of efforts to help vulnerable groups, including those affected by the current energy supply crisis.
He said this when summarising the Selangor Budget 2027 engagement session with the Selangor Menteri Besar at Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC), Section 14 in Shah Alam, today.
Amirudin said the first area of focus in the budget would be finding ways to assist vulnerable groups through a comprehensive support programme ecosystem while strengthening existing aid networks.
However, he said the challenge was to ensure that the support and programmes provided addressed the problems faced by vulnerable groups more accurately and meaningfully.
“Within the framework of looking at vulnerable groups, the groups at the top, or senior citizens and young people, are among those who deserve attention.
“Selangor is facing the challenge of becoming an ageing state in the near future, while every year people’s lifespan is increasing, and the birth rate is relatively…” he said.

Title: Appeals court lets MAIWP strike out man’s bid to change religion from Islam to Sikhism
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Court of Appeal today allowed appeals by the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and the government to strike out a man’s suit challenging his religious status.
The three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid ruled that Shehzad Malik Muhammad Sarwar Malik’s case was a renunciation case and the relief he is seeking could only be granted by the Syariah Court.
“The respondent (Shehzad Malik) here cannot come to the Civil Court as the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to grant the orders,” said Justice Mohd Firuz, who delivered the unanimous decision.
He further said the court took the view that the respondent was legally identified as a person professing the religion of Islam, and the fact that he might not believe in the Islamic faith and did not practise Islamic teaching was irrelevant.
Earlier, the panel dismissed a preliminary objection raised by Shehzad Malik’s counsel contending that the appeals brought by MAIWP and the government were not proper before the court and should be struck out.
Justice Mohd Firuz held that the appeals are competent.
Shedzad Malik filed the originating summons in December 2023, claiming that at the time of his birth in June 1996, his parents professed the religion of Islam, but his mother had raised him as a Sikh.
He said that after his mother died in 2007, he was raised by his uncle, who also professed and practised Sikhism.
He is seeking a court declaration that his religious status according to the National Registration Department’s record be “amended and corrected” to Sikh instead of Islam, and that his name be changed from Shehzad Malik bin Muhammad Sarwar Malik to Bilawal Singh Bhutter.
On Oct 24 last year, the High Court dismissed MAIWP and the government’s applications to strike out the originating summons, prompting them to appeal to the Court of Appeal.
During the proceedings, lawyers Ahmad Kamal Abu Bakar and Arik Zakri Abdul Kadir represented MAIWP while Senior Federal Counsel Husniyyah Hanapi appeared for the government. Lawyers Sachpreetraj Singh Sohanpal and Amanda Sonia Mathew represented Shedzad Malik. — Bernama

Title: In Johor, Indonesian teen charged with trafficking over 25kg of illicit drugs
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 25 — A 19-year-old Indonesian male teenager was charged at the Magistrates’ Court here today with two counts of trafficking illicit drugs, suspected to be heroin and methamphetamine, weighing over 25 kilogrammes (kg) last week.
The accused, Nanda Afrizal, who is employed as a construction worker, nodded to indicate he understood the charges after they were read out before Magistrate Norasidah A. Rahman.
For the first charge, he is alleged to have trafficked drugs suspected to be heroin, with an estimated gross weight of 17,842 grammes, in a room at a house in Taman Lian Seng at 3pm on September 13.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
For the second charge, Nanda is alleged to have trafficked drugs suspected to be methamphetamine, with an estimated gross weight of 8,109 grammes, at the same time and location.
The offense was also framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
Both sections carry either the death penalty or life imprisonment upon conviction.
This includes 12 to 15 strokes of the cane depending on sentencing discretion and if death penalty is imposed.
In a separate charge, Nanda was also accused of possessing drugs suspected to be methamphetamine, with an estimated gross weight of 5.25 grammes, in the living room of the same house at the aforementioned time and date.
The charge was brought under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for illegal possession of drugs and is punishable under Section 39A(1) of the same Act.
The accused faces a prison sentence of not less than two years and not more than five years, as well as whipping of not less than three strokes and not more than nine strokes upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Nik Azman prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
The court did not offer bail and fixed November 25 for mention and submission of the chemistry report.
In the same proceedings, the accused faced a separate charge under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for allegedly remaining in the country without reasonable cause after the expiry of his social visit pass on October 8.
The offence is punishable under Section 15(4) of the same Act, which provides for a fine of not more than RM10,000, imprisonment for up to five years, or both upon conviction.
The accused was sentenced to eight months’ imprisonment from the date of his arrest after he pleaded guilty to the charge.

Title: Anwar wraps China visit with RM36.8b in trade, investment pledges
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, is not just a routine diplomatic trip, but rather a new benchmark for the continuation of strategic relations that strengthen cooperation in various fields between the two countries.
Amidst the global geopolitical and economic uncertainties, the MADANI Diplomacy approach brought by Putrajaya has proven to be fruitful, thus strengthening Malaysia's role as Beijing's main strategic partner in the Southeast Asian region.
The working visit at the invitation of the Chinese government not only strengthens bilateral relations, but also opens up new opportunities for Malaysia to expand investments, export markets and cooperation in strategic and high-value economic areas.
Among the main returns of the visit was the potential investment worth RM28.6 billion from meetings with 26 Chinese companies, including five of the republic's giants, particularly in high-impact sectors such as semiconductors, mainstreaming artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, electric vehicles (EV), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology and advanced manufacturing.
The commitment of companies such as robotics giants AgiBot Innovation, ZTE Corporation, Alibaba Group, Geely Automobile Holdings and Huawei Technologies to increase investment is based on confidence in the stability and policies implemented by the MADANI Government.
Also achieved as a result of this visit was the potential export to China worth RM8.2 billion for a period of one to three years.
Summarising the overall outcome of the visit, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the relationship between Malaysia and China is now at a very strong level and is developing positively.
Describing the close relationship between Malaysia and China today as having gone beyond the usual diplomatic framework, the Prime Minister said this bilateral relationship is based on mutual trust, sincerity and confidence in order to bring prosperity and benefits to the people of both countries.
During the packed working visit, Anwar stressed the long-standing trust and mutual confidence forming the basis of the Malaysia-China bilateral relationship and cooperation that goes beyond traditional diplomatic ties.
The Malaysia-China relationship also translates into a broader agenda covering connectivity, protection of local enterprises, the digital economy, and talent and skills development.
While delivering a keynote address at the plenary session of WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, Anwar said Malaysia has elevated Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) as the core of the country's industrial policy and an instrument of economic transformation, particularly in ensuring talent development goes hand in hand with investment inflows.
"Malaysia and China are well positioned to do more together. Investments come to Malaysia for various reasons. But we all know that it grows especially when there are sufficient skills to support it,” he said.
While in Hangzhou, Malaysia's first-ever participation in the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) provided exposure to the exploration of new technologies and AI applications that deserve to be learned and drawn from China's rapid progress.
Malaysia also offers a stable, well-connected and business-friendly base for partners from China and globally to forge strategic partnerships.
Malaysia's participation in both important Chinese events and Anwar's presence to deliver the keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 and GDTE is a high recognition for Malaysia and the country's leadership.
The Prime Minister had the opportunity to voice his stance on the importance of ethical digital technology, fair and free digital trade and shared prosperity through strategic national cooperation.
Anwar also expressed recognition of China's rapid progress in the fields of digital technology and AI as well as its role in sharing technological advances with countries in the Global South.
The bilateral meeting and discussions between the two Malaysian and Chinese delegations at the West Lake State Guest House, Hangzhou, highlighted the level of personal chemistry between Anwar and China Premier Li Qiang.
The close relationship between the two leaders is not a secret. Repeated meetings since Anwar's tenure as the country's leader in November 2022 reflect a high-level of mutual trust that goes beyond formal diplomatic protocols.
This closeness allows complex issues such as supply chains, the implementation of infrastructure projects and regional and international geopolitical stability to be discussed in a frank and relaxed, yet effective manner.
Among the matters discussed during the bilateral meeting was the agreement between Malaysia and China on the proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, thus providing economic spillover and prosperity to rural areas in Kelantan.
Also given attention was the concerns of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Malaysia regarding foreign market domination that could affect local interests.
"This matter has been raised directly and we have received assurances from the relevant companies, including Alibaba and Li himself, that the best method will be sought so that business dealings do not affect the interests of MSMEs in Malaysia," said Anwar.
This working visit not only maintains China's status as Malaysia's largest trading partner, but also redefines the landscape of cooperation from traditional commodity trade to the digital economy, artificial intelligence and high skills.
China has been Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) for the period January to August this year.
The combination of pragmatic MADANI Diplomacy and the close relationship between Anwar and Li puts Malaysia in the best position to maximise economic benefits for the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Spell out the offence: Aminudin challenges Negeri MB over royal dispute allegations
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution.
Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred.
"What actions were said to have been overlooked? Which provisions of the UUTKNS 1959 were allegedly breached and when did the alleged breach occur?
"If there was an offence, state clearly what it was. If there was a violation of the law, identify the relevant provision. On an issue of this magnitude, the public deserves clear and verifiable facts,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Aminuddin said he was prepared to take responsibility for decisions made during his tenure as Menteri Besar by providing relevant documents, dates and legal provisions based on official records.
Yesterday, Ismail said the issue in the state did not stem from the current administration but was a problem inherited from the previous government.
Meanwhile, the Port Dickson Member of Parliament also questioned Ismail’s decision to sign a proclamation document related to the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, despite previously choosing not to sign the same document.
Aminuddin said the proclamation document dated April 19 was presented to him on April 20 while he was still Menteri Besar, for his signature under Article 10(2) of the UUTKNS 1959.
"I decided not to sign the document. If I, as Menteri Besar at the time, could make that decision due to doubts over the process, how could the signature of the next Menteri Besar appear on the same document?
"Datuk Ismail, with his legal background, would certainly understand the importance of the process. The issue involving Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is about whether the process was properly followed or had flaws from the beginning,” he said.
Aminuddin said Article 10 of the UUTKNS 1959 not only covers matters relating to the powers concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, but also sets out procedures that must be fulfilled, including matters related to a full and complete inquiry. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan Undang, disputed chiefs: Conference of Rulers told of Tunku Nadzaruddin’s succession
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Negeri Sembilan government has notified the Conference of Rulers of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar’s selection as the state’s 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, according to an Undang and three ruling chiefs whose positions are disputed.
The group said the notification meant Tunku Nadzaruddin was the only person with lawful authority to perform the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending meetings of the Conference of Rulers,
The Star
reported today.
It also urged the state administration to recognise Tunku Nadzaruddin and provide him with the privileges and entitlements attached to the office.
“The state government administration must comply and remain loyal and must not commit any act of disobedience.
“The state government administration must also immediately accord all privileges and entitlements prescribed for Tunku Nadzaruddin,” they said.
State civil servants, meanwhile, were urged to follow decisions of the executive council and not bow to pressure from any party.
The group said the official notification to the Conference of Rulers reflected its position that Tunku Nadzaruddin was entitled to exercise all the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
“Through the... official notification to the Conference of Rulers, only Tunku Nadzaruddin... has the lawful authority to exercise all functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending all meetings of the Conference of Rulers,” they said.
The joint statement was issued by Undang of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, whose positions as the Undang of Sungei Ujong, Jelebu and Rembau respectively are disputed.
Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Syed Idrus Al-Qadri was also a signatory.
The group maintains that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir was removed as Yang di-Pertuan Besar on April 19, with Tunku Nadzaruddin subsequently chosen as his successor.
The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang disputes that account, maintaining that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that the April 19 proclamation was invalid.

Title: Negeri Sembilan undangs tell PM, AGC to stay out of state affairs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Negeri Sembilan’s four undangs and the Tunku Besar of Tampin have called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) to refrain from intervening in the state’s affairs, particularly those involving their constitutional prerogatives.
In a press conference in Seremban today, the group said Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 vested the Undang Yang Empat with exclusive authority to appoint and remove the state ruler, Free Malaysia Today reported.
They also cautioned Anwar against using federal agencies in ways that could disrupt the administration of Negeri Sembilan.
“Do not overstep your bounds or intrude where you are not wanted. Do not sow disorder in our state using federal government agencies to paralyse the state government.
“Do not, merely for political gain or influence, or by yielding to pressure from certain quarters, act without reason and conscience, and in doing so violate the principle of constitutional supremacy.
“Do not act beyond your authority and interfere in matters that do not concern you,” they said.
The group said any action they considered unconstitutional would amount to a breach of the prime minister’s oath under the Sixth Schedule of the Federal Constitution, as well as a breach of trust under Article 71(1) and (2) and the principle of federalism.
They also turned their attention to outside parties, especially opposition political parties, warning them against “fishing in muddied waters” or “twisting the facts” through disparaging remarks about the state government and adat, or customs.
“No political party has the power to remove any ruler,” they said. “That power is vested solely in its rightful authority, and in the context of Negeri Sembilan, it falls within the power of the Undang Yang Empat.”
The group said Negeri Sembilan’s customs had been practised for more than 500 years and maintained that their role as custodians of those traditions gave them the best understanding of them.
“Only the jeweller knows the gem,” they said.
They further maintained that selecting and removing the Yang di-Pertuan Besar was a customary prerogative protected by Articles 7, 10 and 11 of the state constitution.
The undangs also rejected claims that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and the state executive council were responsible for Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir’s purported removal, describing the allegation as “malicious slander” driven by the personal interests of certain groups.
According to them, Ismail and the exco members were only fulfilling their constitutional obligation to act on the undangs’ decision under Article 10.
The statement came from Undang of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and was jointly issued with Datuk Mubarak Dohak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad and Abdul Rahim Yasin, whose positions as the Undangs of Sungei Ujong, Jelebu and Rembau are disputed.
The statement follows Anwar’s criticism on Wednesday of Ismail and the former exco over several issues concerning the royal institution that had become contentious in the state.
The exco had earlier, on September 16, said Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar in April was legitimate and declared Tunku Nadzaruddin the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan, with Ismail endorsing the position the following day.
The state’s Dewan Keadilan dan Undang subsequently disputed that position, saying the exco’s decision carried no legal effect and that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The dispute intensified on September 17 when the AGC said the proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar was invalid, rejecting it alongside the exco’s subsequent endorsement of the proclamation.
The AGC also said the menteri besar and the exco members at the time could not act on their own to remove the state ruler.
Three days later, Tuanku Muhriz withdrew the appointments of all 10 exco members, with breaches of their oaths of office cited as the reason.

Title: Najib may walk out of Kajang Prison next month if High Court stays 15-year 1MDB sentence and RM50m fine is paid, says lawyer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could leave Kajang Prison as early as next month to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest if the High Court grants a stay of his 15-year 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) sentence, his lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said today.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Shafee said the move could take place if the court grants the stay on October 14 and the RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of Najib’s conditional pardon is paid.
The High Court has fixed October 14 to hear Najib’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case pending his appeal.
Asked how soon Najib could return home to serve his sentence under house arrest if all the required conditions were met, Shafee said it would depend on whether the necessary preparations had been completed.
“If we are ready, say on October 14 we obtain the stay of sentence and then, God willing, the RM50 million is paid, there is a strong possibility that he could be released on the same day,” he told reporters after court proceedings involving Najib.
“Or there may be arguments in court as to whether his release takes effect on the same day,” he said.
Shafee said the defence had sought the stay of the 1MDB sentence following the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
He said the legal team had previously not sought a stay when Najib was convicted in the 1MDB case because he was already serving his sentence for the SRC International case.
“However, the conditional pardon has changed the situation because the 1MDB sentence could affect Najib’s efforts to serve his SRC International sentence under house arrest,” he said.
“If the SRC sentence ends, the 1MDB sentence will begin, which is why we are seeking the stay, so that the stay has an effect,” he added.
Najib has appealed against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abusing his position and 21 money laundering charges involving RM2.27 billion in 1MDB funds.
The 15-year prison term imposed in the 1MDB case is to begin after he completes his sentence in the SRC International case.

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia form joint Halal Council to strengthen bilateral trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council in a bid to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today.
He added that the council would be chaired by Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) with Malaysia serving as its secretary-general, and the first meeting would be held in October this year.
"Next month, the focus is on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to ease bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today.
Ahmad Zahid said the council would build on existing bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia to address differing halal requirements, repeated procedures and difficulties faced by businesses seeking to enter neighbouring markets.
Malaysia and Indonesia signed a memorandum of cooperation in 2023, while bilateral negotiations on facilitating halal certification and trade between the two countries were concluded in June this year, he said.
He said closer bilateral cooperation could identify practical ways to facilitate trade, reduce duplication and connect businesses to regional supply chains.
Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia brings experience in standards, governance, Islamic finance and trade facilitation, while Indonesia offers scale, production capacity and entrepreneurship, which are at the core of halal diplomacy, where both parties can leverage the trust built to open markets, facilitate investment and create opportunities together.
He added that such cooperation should ultimately translate into fewer barriers, easier market access and more companies trading across borders.
He said small manufacturers should have a clearer route to overseas buyers, while halal-certified companies should receive the support needed to fulfil their first export orders.
"The future of halal will depend on how effectively we connect ourselves and build that trust in the future,” he said, adding that Malaysia aims to increase its halal exports to about RM80 billion by 2030.
Ahmad Zahid noted that the halal industry contributed about 11 per cent to Malaysia’s gross domestic product, yet only about 14.7 per cent of halal-certified companies were exporters.
"To realise our ambition, we must help more of these companies compete abroad. Certification is only the beginning of that journey. Companies also need consistent production, suitable packaging, working capital, reliable logistics and an understanding of their target markets,” he added.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid shared that the International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) 2026 has attracted US$1.2 billion in sales over the first two days.
Hosted by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry and organised by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, MIHAS 2026 is being held from Sept 23 to Sept 26, 2026.
Ahmad Zahid hopes that sales and sales potential will continue to increase until MIHAS ends on Sunday, as the annual organisation of MIHAS has established the event as a global halal exhibition brand, despite several countries also organising similar exhibitions. — Bernama

Title: Bandar Utama school stabbing: Family plans civil suit as mother asks if tragedy could have been prevented
Article:
KEPONG, Sept 25 — More than 11 months after her daughter was fatally stabbed at school, Wong Lee Ping is still asking a question she cannot put behind her: could the tragedy have been prevented?
The mother of 16-year-old Yap Shing Xuen said the family is planning to pursue a civil suit as the criminal case moves to the appeal stage following the Shah Alam High Court’s decision to acquit the teenage accused on the grounds of unsoundness of mind.
“Our lawyers will be filing a civil suit. Until the criminal proceedings are completed, we will not comment on the details. Our lawyers will explain those matters later,” Wong told a press conference today.
Asked whether the civil action would be filed after the appeal or concurrently, Wong said the family intended to proceed but had yet to determine when.
She also confirmed that the family was considering legal action against certain parties, but declined to identify them, saying the matter would be reviewed in due course.
For Wong, however, the civil action is not simply another legal avenue. Her daughter, she said, is not coming home.
“I am not here today to seek resolution in the criminal case, because my daughter is already gone.
“No matter what we do today, I will never be able to hear her call me again. I will never be able to call her home again,” she said, breaking down in tears.
‘Were the warning signs seen?’
Wong said she remained troubled by what might have happened before the stabbing.
“If there were already some warning signs before the tragedy happened, were those warning signs seen?
“And if they were seen, did anyone actually take sufficient action?” she said.
Wong said she was not asking schools to guarantee that tragedies would never happen.
“But I hope that whenever a child shows warning signs of danger, we don’t wait until another child loses their life before regretting it and asking why nobody stopped it, why nobody could stop it.
“My daughter does not have a second chance,” she said.
Wong said she hoped her daughter’s death could instead give other children a better chance of being protected.
“That is why I am continuing to stand here and speak today,” she said.
She also questioned whether warning signs had been missed during the accused teenager’s first two weeks at the school.
“For two weeks the student brought a knife to school, why didn’t anyone notice this? I think it is very possible that other students knew.
“Why didn’t the school teachers tell the children that if they noticed anything dangerous, or if someone brought a knife or something like that to school, they should tell a teacher?” she said.
Wong’s husband, How Boon Chin, who was also at the press conference, stressed the importance of measures to prevent similar incidents in schools.
“School is supposed to be a very safe place,” he said.
Wong Lee Ping and How Boon Chin, the parents of 16-year-old student Yap Shing Xuen, who was fatally stabbed at a Bandar Utama school last year, stand alongside Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng (2nd left) and supporters during a press conference at the Kepong MP Service Centre in Kuala Lumpur on September 25, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
From murder charge to appeal
Yap Shing Xuen was fatally stabbed at a secondary school in Bandar Utama on October 14 last year.
The teenager accused of killing her, who was 14 at the time, was charged with murder at the Petaling Jaya Magistrates’ Court on October 22.
The case subsequently went through psychiatric assessment before being transferred to the Shah Alam High Court, where the trial was conducted in camera because the accused was a minor.
A psychiatric assessment found him fit to stand trial in January. He pleaded not guilty when the murder charge was read again at the High Court on February 12.
The trial began on August 3.
On August 13, the High Court ordered the teenager to enter his defence after finding that the prosecution had established a prima facie case.
The defence closed its case on August 26 after two witnesses — the accused and a forensic psychiatrist — testified.
On September 14, High Court Judge Adlin Abdul Majid acquitted and discharged the teenager after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the offence, and ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.
The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) filed a Notice of Appeal at the Court of Appeal on September 22, challenging the acquittal.
Appeal puts High Court ruling under fresh scrutiny
Kepong DAP MP Lim Lip Eng, whose office offered legal assistance to the family, said the AGC’s decision to appeal showed that prosecutors were challenging the High Court’s ruling.
“And to answer a few questions from the reporters whether we or the family members agree with the judgment, I think the government has answered. The government disagrees with the judgment, hence the appeal,” he said.
Wong said the family was moved by the decision to appeal.
“When I heard that the AGC was appealing, I was actually very touched because I felt that someone was supporting me,” she said.
She said the family would now wait for the appeal process rather than attempt to intervene in matters outside its control.
Wong also said the family had not had the opportunity to access certain documentary evidence, including government documents and the medical report.
She therefore declined to comment on some aspects of the case while the appeal was pending, saying the Court of Appeal should make its decision based on the complete evidence.
Asked whether the family was willing to meet the accused again, Wong said she had no intention of doing so.
“I don’t think I will meet him again, there is no need for that,” she said.
‘It feels like it happened only the day before yesterday’
The passage of almost a year has not made the loss feel distant for Wong.
She said she had struggled to return to work after her daughter’s death, continuing only because her team was still there.
“We reduced our workload. We worked more slowly and did less,” she said.
“It feels as though this happened only the day before yesterday.”
For much of the past year, she said, she simply wanted to rest and not think about anything.
“Just eat and sleep. The year passed like that,” she added.
Wong said she had spent the year carrying out Buddhist prayers and rituals for her daughter, including ceremonies marking the 49th and 100th days after her death.
She also arranged for 20,000 copies of Buddhist scriptures to be printed and distributed to temples.
But Wong said the family had to be careful about how much of the case they discussed with her other daughter.
“There are many things that I don’t talk to her about too much because it would disturb her life and affect her, and it would also affect me,” Wong said.
“Because in our current situation, it feels like a second trauma for us.
“So I try to avoid exposing her to these things. I only discuss important matters with her. Other things, I don’t tell her too much.”
Wong said she was grateful for the public support the family had received throughout the case.
“The public has really shown us a lot of care and support. I am really touched. I thank everyone and am grateful that people have shown us this support,” she said.
How said the family would hold a separate press conference on the civil suit once more details were available.

Title: KTMB apologises after absent staff strands 25 riders at Anak Bukit station
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has apologised to affected passengers following an incident in which the Anak Bukit Station main gate failed to open as scheduled early this morning.
KTMB said preliminary investigations found that the station was scheduled to begin operations at 5.30 am, but the staff member assigned to work failed to report for duty due to health reasons.
“Upon being informed at about 5.55 am that the station gate was still locked, the officer on duty tried to contact the staff member concerned but was unsuccessful.
“Immediate action was taken by instructing a counter clerk from a nearby station, who was scheduled to report for duty at 7 am, to arrive earlier at Anak Bukit Station,” KTMB said in a statement.
It said the replacement staff member arrived at 6.30 am and the station’s main gate was successfully opened.
Preliminary checks found that an estimated 25 passengers were affected and missed two KTM Komuter services, namely Train 2901 and Train 2903, which were scheduled to depart from Anak Bukit Station at 5.58 am and 6.18 am, respectively.
KTMB stressed that it took the incident seriously and was conducting a further investigation in accordance with existing procedures, while assuring that station access according to operating hours, as well as passenger safety and comfort, remained its priorities. — Bernama

Title: ‘Suspicion cannot take the place of proof’: BFM ordered to pay ex-presenter RM358,400 over 2019 dismissal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Industrial Court has ordered BFM Media Sdn Bhd to pay former producer and presenter Umapagan Ampikaipakan RM358,400 after ruling that the radio station failed to prove the misconduct allegations used to justify his dismissal in 2019.
While the allegations against Umapagan were serious, Industrial Court chairman Pravin Kaur Jessy found that BFM had not proved the alleged misconduct on the balance of probabilities,
The Edge Malaysia
reported yesterday.
BFM had accused Umapagan of sexual harassment and other misconduct, including sending explicit messages, making inappropriate remarks and engaging in unwanted physical contact. He denied the allegations.
In a 98-page judgment, Pravin found shortcomings in both the charges and the evidence relied upon by the company, including a lack of specific dates and names in some allegations and the absence of original message exchanges.
She said an employer was required to prove the misconduct as charged rather than rely on a broader impression of an employee’s behaviour.
“This court cannot permit a vague charge to be cured by evidential accretion after the event. The company was required to prove the misconduct as charged, not a general impression that the claimant was tactile or overly familiar,” she said.
Pravin said that, taken as a whole, BFM’s case had fallen short despite the gravity of the accusations.
“Having considered the evidence in its entirety, the court is driven to one conclusion. The company’s case, though grave in allegation, was not made good in proof,” she said.
She added that too many of the allegations were imprecise, uncertain in attribution, inadequately documented or insufficiently tested.
“Suspicion may have justified inquiry. Concern may have justified caution. But neither suspicion nor concern can take the place of proof.
“On the evidence before it, the court is not satisfied that the misconduct relied upon has been established on a balance of probabilities,” she said.
Umapagan had argued that his dismissal was without just cause or excuse and alleged that it was made in bad faith, amounted to victimisation and constituted an unfair labour practice.
BFM maintained that the dismissal was justified.
According to
The Edge Malaysia
, the parties also disputed when Umapagan began working for the station. He said he had been employed there since 2009, while BFM said he joined in April 2014.
BFM also disputed his claim of having an unblemished employment record, citing a previous warning over inappropriate communication with an intern.
The company said two external lawyers familiar with Malaysian employment law had carried out an independent investigation into the allegations and that management did not interfere with the process.
Umapagan was issued a show-cause letter on December 24, 2018, and dismissed on January 4, 2019.
With reinstatement no longer an option, the court accepted April 2014 as his starting date for the purpose of calculating compensation.
It awarded him RM51,200 in compensation in lieu of reinstatement, equivalent to one month’s salary of RM12,800 for each of four completed years of service.
He was also awarded RM307,200 in back wages, representing the maximum 24 months permitted under the Second Schedule of the Industrial Relations Act 1967.
The awards totalled RM358,400.

Title: Immigration busts Indonesians making RM50,000 monthly via illegal beauty treatments
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department (JIM) detained seven Indonesian nationals believed to be working as beauty therapists in a special operation at four locations in Shah Alam, Pandan Perdana and Kepong last Wednesday.
JIM, in a statement today, said those detained comprised one man and six women aged between 19 and 44.
The operation, which began at 12.15 pm, involved personnel from the Intelligence and Special Operations Division of the Immigration Department headquarters in Putrajaya, with the cooperation of the Pharmacy Enforcement Division from the Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Health Departments.
“Based on public information and a month-long intelligence gathering, the operation team was deployed to the residential premises.
“The team also seized medicines, treatment and beauty equipment, a mobile phone and RM400 cash believed to be proceeds from the activity,” the statement said.
JIM said the group was believed to have offered beauty and aesthetic services, mainly to Indonesians in the Klang Valley, through social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.
Customers were required to make appointments before receiving the services, which were carried out at rented residential premises to evade detection by the authorities.
The department said the activity was believed to have been operating since last year and could generate up to RM50,000 in monthly income, depending on the number of customers and services provided.
JIM said two women and a man were detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while three women were detained under Section 6(1)(c) of the same Act. Another woman was detained under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
All seven will also be investigated by the Ministry of Health for alleged offences involving possession of unregistered products under Regulations 7(1) and 30(1) of the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina: SMKA Jempol to become first TVET religious school in Malaysia
Article:
JEMPOL, Sept 25 — Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama (SMKA) Jempol will become the country’s first Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) religious-stream school.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the school was being built at a cost of RM98 million on a 14.22-hectare site over a three-year period under the 12th Malaysia Plan.
“Previously, TVET was offered only at vocational colleges or regular schools; we will now bring this TVET model to SMKA Jempol. Insya-Allah, SMKA Jempol will be the first SMKA to adopt or introduce TVET.
“I hope the project can be completed within the stipulated timeframe so that we can immediately develop TVET education to meet not only the needs of the industry, but also the needs of the country at present,” she told reporters after officiating at the groundbreaking ceremony for the construction of SMKA Jempol here today.
Fadhlina said the fully residential school would be equipped with an administration block, an academic block with 25 classrooms, laboratories, workshops, a library, hall, canteen and prayer hall, as well as other facilities and a hostel with a capacity for 720 students.
Meanwhile, she said religious school students in the country were also encouraged to master various languages as an important medium for strengthening the dakwah agenda more effectively.
Taking the example of SMKA Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin in Penang, which has been recognised as Malaysia’s first ‘dakwah school’, Fadhlina said its students were given exposure to Chinese, Tamil, English and Arabic, in addition to Malay.
“Children in religious schools will certainly master Malay as the main language. At the same time, they must also be given emphasis on other languages.
“We see that these children have the ability to master more than one language. Language is one of the tools that must be mastered to convey matters related to dakwah and explanations about Islam more effectively,” she said.
Fadhlina said the ministry also placed emphasis on character development, values of trustworthiness and integrity among students to prepare them to face current challenges.
She said education should not focus solely on academic achievement, but also encompass intellectual development, cultivating a reading culture and fostering leadership with integrity.
“The need to reject corruption and uphold clean leadership must be taught and emphasised from an early age.
“That is why religious schools have special programmes such as Nadwah Kepimpinan Islam, which are expected to produce future leaders, particularly Muslim leaders with character and who uphold religious values,” she said.
She said the development of religious education institutions involved more than merely the construction of physical infrastructure, but also aimed to instil human values in students so that they would become a principled generation capable of contributing to society. — Bernama
